sites.name: Connecting Ridge
sites.note: High ridge linking Shackleton and de Gerlache craters (Site01).

sites.name: Shackleton Rim
sites.note: Rim of Shackleton crater, almost exactly at the pole (Site04).

sites.name: Peak near Shackleton
sites.note: Elevated region between Shackleton and Slater craters (Site07).

sites.name: de Gerlache-Kocher Massif
sites.note: Massif between de Gerlache and Kocher craters (Site42).

sites.name: Malapert Massif
sites.note: ~5 km high massif on the Earth-facing side of the pole (Site23).

sites.name: Leibnitz Beta Plateau
sites.note: Plateau region, later refined into the Mons Mouton candidates (Site20).

sites.name: IM-2 Athena (Mons Mouton)
sites.note: Intuitive Machines, 6 March 2025: southernmost landing so far, on the Mons Mouton plateau.

sites.name: IM-1 Odysseus (Malapert A)
sites.note: Intuitive Machines, 22 February 2024: first commercial soft landing, on a ~12 deg slope.

sites.name: Blue Ghost 1 (Mare Crisium)
sites.note: Firefly Aerospace, 2 March 2025: first fully successful commercial landing.

sites.name: Chandrayaan-3 (Shiv Shakti)
sites.note: ISRO, 2023: high southern latitude, but Earth is always in view.

sites.name: SLIM (Shioli crater)
sites.note: JAXA, 19 January 2024: the 'Moon Sniper' pinpoint landing.

sites.name: Chang'e 4 (Von Kármán, far side)
sites.note: CNSA, 2019: on the far side Earth never rises, so all radio goes through the Queqiao relay.

sites.name: Chang'e 6 (Apollo basin, far side)
sites.note: CNSA, 2024: first far-side sample return; no direct line of sight to Earth.

sites.name: Apollo 11 (Tranquility Base)
sites.note: Equatorial: Earth hangs high in the sky, Sun rises and sets every ~29.5 days.

sites.name: Apollo 14 (Fra Mauro)
sites.note: Near side, close to the equator: Earth stays high, roughly two weeks of day and night.
